Do you think you are a smart shopper? Well, you may think you are, but hold on! There are various marketing strategies which ⓐinfluences your decisions. ⓑLearning about them will make you a smarter shopper.

Hunger Marketing
Junho: What? The sale ends in two hours? If I don't buy the sneakers now, I will have ⓒto buying them at a higher price.
Stop, Junho! You're buying the sneakers just ⓓbecause of you don't want to miss the sale. You're falling for a hunger marketing strategy.
If people can buy a product only for a limited time, they often feel "hungry" for it and want to buy it. About ⓔmissing the sale, don't worry, Junho. You'll soon see a similar sale again.

Wait, Yuna! You only want the dress because you saw (A)[it / them] again and again on social media. It isn't just you. There are a lot of people (B)[which / who] fall for a viral marketing strategy. Why?
Information about a product can spread quickly and widely on the Internet, just like a "virus." If a product becomes hot on social media, people naturally want to have it. Yuna, just remember (C)[that / which] a popular product isn't always right for you.

questions.question:
다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 ⓐ, ⓑ에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

Somi: I'm looking for a lipstick for my mom.
Salesperson: How about this?
Somi: Expensive! I thought I could buy a lipstick for 30 dollars.
Salesperson: This is also popular.
Somi: That's better!
Hold on, Somi! Your budget is 30 dollars, but you are buying a 40-dollar lipstick. The 40-dollar lipstick sounds cheap only because the salesperson showed you a 50-dollar lipstick first. This is an example of the anchoring effect.
Usually, the first piece of information becomes an "anchor" and influences the shopper's decision. In your case, the 50-dollar lipstick was the anchor. Somi, don't just rely on the first piece of information that is given to you.

We should be careful not to make the mistake of thinking other products are ⓐ__________ to buy by using the first product as the ⓑ__________.
questions.explanation: 소미는 첫 번째 본 50달러짜리 립스틱을 기준으로 40달러짜리 립스틱이 싸게 여겨 예산이 30달러였음에도 40달러짜리 립스틱을 구매하고 있는 사례를 통해, 첫 번째 정보가 '닻'이 되어 구매자의 결정에 영향을 미치는 것을 설명하고 있다. 따라서 ⓐ에는 '합리적인'을 뜻하는 reasonable, ⓑ에는 '기준'을 뜻하는 basis가 적절하다.
